title: Demeter — What the myth explains
summary: Demeter, goddess of grain and harvest, is central to the Eleusinian Mysteries. This study reads the myth as an answer to a question.
body:
Demeter, goddess of grain and harvest, is central to the Eleusinian Mysteries. Her grief over Persephone's abduction brings winter.

Myths answer questions science had not yet asked: why the seasons turn, why suffering exists, why kings rule. Demeter encodes its culture's answers in narrative form — explanations you can remember because they move you. Viewed through a narrative lens, Demeter is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

To ask what Demeter explains is to recover the curiosity that made it. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Hades and Pegasus.
